<p>Some Xreal smart glasses have been discounted as part of a Black Friday promotion. This includes the recently-released Xreal One Pro glasses. The smart specs <a data-i13n="elm:affiliate_link;sellerN:Amazon;elmt:;cpos:1;pos:1" href="https://shopping.yahoo.com/rdlw?merchantId=66ea567a-c987-4c2e-a2ff-02904efde6ea&amp;itemId=amazon_B0FDPNC49S&amp;siteId=us-engadget&amp;pageId=1p-autolink&amp;contentUuid=ceac0418-a64d-4a6c-bc53-d3e89f22267d&amp;featureId=text-link&amp;merchantName=Amazon&amp;linkText=are+down+to+%24599&amp;custData=eyJzb3VyY2VOYW1lIjoiV2ViLURlc2t0b3AtVmVyaXpvbiIsImxhbmRpbmdVcmwiOiJodHRwczovL3d3dy5hbWF6b24uY29tL1hSRUFMLUdsYXNzZXMtWC1QcmlzbS1EaXNwbGF5LUFuZHJvaWQvZHAvQjBGRFBOQzQ5Uy8_&amp;signature=AQAAAfKr-5_HHaqSFYstmjrOfQXQiqwoxhC19IFxWSGdWqV3&amp;gcReferrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.amazon.com%2FXREAL-Glasses-X-Prism-Display-Android%2Fdp%2FB0FDPNC49S%2F" class="rapid-with-clickid" data-original-link="https://www.amazon.com/XREAL-Glasses-X-Prism-Display-Android/dp/B0FDPNC49S/?th=1">are down to $599</a>, which is $50 off. The sale applies to both sizes.</p> 
<p>These glasses <a data-i13n="cpos:2;pos:1" href="https://www.engadget.com/home/home-theater/xreals-new-one-pro-ar-glasses-are-surprisingly-good-143034826.html">are the real deal</a>. We praised them <a data-i13n="cpos:3;pos:1" href="https://www.engadget.com/ar-vr/xreals-one-pro-intrigues-me-in-ways-metas-smart-glasses-dont-120000554.html">in our official review</a>, saying they offer similar functionality to the Apple Vision Pro, but at a much friendlier price point. Wearing these glasses allows access to a massive 222-inch virtual display that can be used for just about anything. The glasses connect to laptops, gaming consoles and smartphones, among other gadgets.</p> <span id="end-legacy-contents"></span>
<p>
 </p> 
<p>The 1080p Micro-OLED screens are surprisingly bright and sharp, which makes this device great for both work and consuming content. The frames even darken to give the illusion of wearing sunglasses.</p> 
<p>The glasses are light and comfortable, especially when compared to the Vision Pro. However, the comfort does come at a price. These oversized glasses are not as immersive as Apple's product, because they don't completely block out light and cover the entire face. They offer a 57-degree field of view. This is squarely an augmented reality product and not a virtual reality product.</p> 
<p>The company has also discounted its <a data-i13n="elm:affiliate_link;sellerN:Amazon;elmt:;cpos:4;pos:1" href="https://shopping.yahoo.com/rdlw?merchantId=66ea567a-c987-4c2e-a2ff-02904efde6ea&amp;itemId=amazon_B0F7R96TFC&amp;siteId=us-engadget&amp;pageId=1p-autolink&amp;contentUuid=ceac0418-a64d-4a6c-bc53-d3e89f22267d&amp;featureId=text-link&amp;merchantName=Amazon&amp;linkText=Xreal+One+AR+glasses+to+%24399&amp;&amp;signature=AQAAAfTxxkRs4V656cgcK7-1gM-ne4RW9O8K9UKhGbYl1GBT&amp;gcReferrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.amazon.com%2FXREAL-Glasses-Display-Expertly-Android%2Fdp%2FB0F7R96TFC%2F" class="rapid-with-clickid" data-original-link="https://www.amazon.com/XREAL-Glasses-Display-Expertly-Android/dp/B0F7R96TFC/?th=1">Xreal One AR glasses to $399</a>, which is a discount of around $100. These offer smaller virtual screens than the Pro, with a 50-degree field of view. Elsewhere in the smart glasses space, the <a data-i13n="elm:affiliate_link;sellerN:Amazon;elmt:;cpos:5;pos:1" href="https://shopping.yahoo.com/rdlw?merchantId=66ea567a-c987-4c2e-a2ff-02904efde6ea&amp;itemId=amazon_B0CGXX2HG5&amp;siteId=us-engadget&amp;pageId=1p-autolink&amp;contentUuid=ceac0418-a64d-4a6c-bc53-d3e89f22267d&amp;featureId=text-link&amp;merchantName=Amazon&amp;linkText=Meta+Ray+Ban+Gen+1+glasses&amp;&amp;signature=AQAAAV9Fp-DzEuH1qes2vXViMDK6nSrpv-fXzizKCXdVsX0m&amp;gcReferrer=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.amazon.com%2FMeta-Ray-Ban-Glasses-Wayfarer-Frames%2Fdp%2FB0CGXX2HG5%2F" class="rapid-with-clickid" data-original-link="https://www.amazon.com/Meta-Ray-Ban-Glasses-Wayfarer-Frames/dp/B0CGXX2HG5/?th=1">Meta Ray Ban Gen 1 glasses</a> are 20 percent off for Black Friday as well.</p>
